page: Google Cloud Platform e2-medium is an entry-level, shared-core virtual machine instance belonging to the E2 family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to a single shared physical Intel Xeon core with 2 threads, operating at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is provisioned with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, and does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate that the shared-core architecture limits sustained multi-core performance. While the stress-ng single-core CPU performance registers in the average range at 2642.19, the multi-core CPU performance drops to the bottom 25% with a score of 2642.78, reflecting the constraints of shared CPU allocation. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached read and write speeds measuring 6.36 GB/sec and 4.83 GB/sec respectively, placing it in the bottom 10% of tested configurations. Geekbench scores further confirm low-intensity capabilities, with a single-core score of 661.0 and a multi-core score of 682.0.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-medium offers a highly economical profile for workloads that do not require continuous, high-performance CPU utilization. The shared-resource model provides a low-cost entry point for lightweight applications, but the lack of dedicated physical cores and low memory bandwidth make it unsuitable for resource-intensive databases, heavy data processing, or production-grade LLM inference. It is best suited for low-traffic web serving, microservices, development environments, and basic background tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-medium is a shared-core virtual machine instance designed for budget-conscious, low-intensity workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.2 GHz, it provides 2 vCPUs backed by a single shared physical core and 4.0 GB of system memory. The instance lacks local storage and dedicated GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks reflect its shared-resource architecture, with stress-ng single-core metrics in the average tier, while multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into the lower percentiles. This resource profile makes the e2-medium a cost-effective option for development environments, lightweight microservices, and low-traffic web serving, though it is not suited for sustained high-compute or memory-intensive tasks.
